newsitem.title: GERMANY: Douglas targets record earnings in '97.
newsitem.headline: Douglas targets record earnings in '97.

text.p: German cosmetics and drugstore chain Douglas Holding AG said on Wednesday that group sales in the first five months of this year were up 5.7 percent to 1.57 billion marks ($909.9 million), while earnings were just down on last year.

Chief executive Joern Kreke told Douglas' annual shareholders meeting the company would devote all its efforts this year to break a run of stagnant results and beat its previous record profit of 227 million marks in 1993.
Kreke, according to the text of a speech he gave to the AGM, said that five-month sales were up 4.2 percent in Germany but had gained by 15.1 percent abroad.
Same-store sales were up by 0.64 percent -- little changed in Germany but up 5.7 percent outside Germany.

Operating earnings so far this year, not counting proceeds from the disposal of the Stilke unit, were slightly down due to a higher advertising spend. Douglas expects to recoup through increased sales in the busier months of the year, Kreke said.
Sales in 1996, announced in April, rose 3.1 percent to 4.3 billion marks and group net profits were up 2.1 percent at 105.6 million marks.
Earnings per share, based on the DVFA accounting rule, rose to 2.95 marks from 2.80, and the company proposed a dividend unchanged at 1.40 marks.
